For a complete pad-capacitance workflow, use a PDK notebook from [Choose a simulation](../examples.qmd#getting-started).
Q3D solves the geometry Palace meshes: `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` builds the
plan's SGB model and writes a handoff that carries it. There are no
hand-written bodies and no Region padding; the Region is the plan's
`VACUUM_REGION`.

## GeometryPlan-backed C/G preparation

The shared [Xmon input lesson](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd) prepares an
immutable `snapshot` with its final Net assignments and its
`set_vacuum_region(...)`. The frontend builds that snapshot's SGB model and
prepares a capacitance-only handoff.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import MatrixRunControl, prepare_q3d_from_geometry

AEDT_VERSION = "2024.2"  # Choose explicitly: 2023.2 or 2024.2.

handoff = prepare_q3d_from_geometry(
    snapshot,
    aedt_version=AEDT_VERSION,
    modeling="solid",
    output_dir=Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-q3d-cg"),
    project_name="public_xmon_q3d_cg",
    design_name="PublicXmonQ3dCg",
    net_types={"xmon_pad": "Signal", "Ground": "Signal"},
    physical_ground_nets=("Ground",),
    run_control=MatrixRunControl(
        "Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3,
    ),
)
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.archive_path)
```

What the call does with its inputs:

- `modeling="solid"` builds the conductors as solids (SGB Route C);
  `"thin_film"` builds them as sheets (Route A).
- `net_types` gives every Net of the model its Q3D type, keyed by Net ID, and
  must name exactly the model's Nets. Here both Nets are `Signal`, so both stay
  in the matrix.
- `physical_ground_nets` records which Nets are physically ground,
  independently of their Q3D type.
- Each Net becomes one `Q3dNetSpec` over the model's conductor objects of that
  Net, named by its AEDT name (the Net ID with every character outside
  `[A-Za-z0-9_]` replaced). Two Nets that would share an AEDT name are refused.
- The materials are the stack's records; the handoff carries the model's STEP,
  BREP, sidecar and guard in its `model/` folder.

The 6 GHz frequency and three-pass limit are study inputs. Preserve actual
extraction criteria, any changes and native completion/convergence status in
your study notes. The
[result-reading lesson](returned-results.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use) relates
the selected matrix quantity and its available history to the intended SCQ
use; the native stopping flag alone does not decide its adequacy. The
[matrix observation contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations)
describes how native status, reported delta and actual controls are kept with
the matrix.

## Know which formulation you requested

Q3D on the SGB model extracts capacitance and conductance only. It returns the
native `results/q3d/c_matrix.csv` and creates no AC-RL or DC setup. AC/RL is not available in this version; it is tracked in
[issue #265](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/265).

A dedicated grounded Region enclosure is an additional optional choice:
`grounded_region_net="EnclosureGround"`, where the new Net name
differs from all model Nets. It requests six native PEC face sheets and
preserves the model's Nets. It does not unite the sheets, add bridges or claim
an AC/DC return path. The
[contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q3d-extraction-and-region-ground-candidate)
owns native validation/readback and the distinction between enclosure and
physical ground. Changing enclosure or extraction formulation creates a
different experiment, not an offline update to old results.

## Build only, then solve

The native build-only operation uses the existing CLI with the prepared
handoff: `python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only`
(substitute the directory returned by `prepare_q3d_from_geometry`). It imports
the model, assigns the Nets, Region and setup, reads them back,
saves the project and releases its owned Desktop without calling `Analyze` or
exporting C/G matrices. This consumes the one-shot handoff; prepare a new
handoff before a later solve. The normal `--execute` path solves and returns
the matrix. The [Q3D contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q3d-sgb-model)
describes the import, the receipt and strict result reading.

Use the `aedt-epr` installation extra on the machine that prepares the
handoff: it brings the GDSFactory/KLayout source and OCP, which exports the SGB
STEP. Configured resource values are recorded run
inputs; they do not by themselves guarantee a hard process-memory cap or report
an independently observed effective solver allocation.
